dialogue.content: compared this month to last month and stopped comparing.
put a card in a drawer as a strategy.
checked a bill I already knew the amount of.
opened a second savings account and left it empty.
added up subscriptions on a napkin. stopped at nine.
saved up for something small out of the main account.
checked the balance and closed the app again.
past about four separately named pots the money stops being one lump. each one has a purpose attached, and I won't break into a pot for something that isn't its purpose.
below four it's just savings, and savings is spendable.
moved a direct debit date by three days.
found a charge I didn't recognise. it was me.
rounded up the change jar into the account.
read a thread about interest rates and learned nothing.
compared two accounts for twenty minutes and switched neither.
cancelled a thing and immediately got an email offering a discount.
filed the receipts I'd been carrying around for a month.
every goal I've actually funded had its own named pot. the ones I was saving for out of the general account, I never once got to — the money was always there and always went elsewhere.
not one, over about six years.
updated the card details on one service and forgot the rest.
checked whether a refund had landed. it hadn't.
looked at last month's total and looked away again.
